topic_ko: 알고리즘이 설계한 디지털 환경에서 인간의 주체성 지키기
_note: 정답 분산: theme③, gist⑤, title②, claim④, implication①, blank③, order②, insert③, summary⑤. grammar/vocab/irrelevant는 위치 종속.

passage: Behavioral economists use the term choice architecture for the way a decision setting shapes the decisions made inside it.
In digital life, that setting is built almost entirely by algorithms.
They decide which posts appear, which products are suggested, and which options are visible at all.
Through that quiet editing, they push users toward certain routes rather than others.
Sometimes the push is helpful, steering people toward healthier habits.
But when the designers' aims differ from the user's welfare, the same push becomes manipulation.
Guarding one's own judgment therefore takes deliberate work: seeking out unfamiliar viewpoints and refusing the obvious recommendation.
It also takes remembering that an algorithm's data records what has already happened, not what ought to happen next.

passage: The design of the space in which we choose has a powerful hold on what we end up choosing.
Online, algorithms occupy that designer's chair.
By selecting what we see and what we are offered, they steer us down particular paths.
Such steering can be kind, nudging us toward better habits.
It can also be self-serving, when the designer's goals and the user's welfare come apart.
Protecting our own judgment therefore requires conscious, ongoing effort.
We have to look for views the system would never suggest and choose against its predictions.
And we must recall that algorithmic data mirrors the past, not a plan for how we should live.

알고리즘이 설계한 환경에서 주체적 판단을 지키려면 의식적 노력이 필요하다.
gist.explanation_ko: 알고리즘이 선택 환경을 설계하므로, 다양한 관점을 찾고 추천에 맞서는 의식적 노력이 필요하다는 것이 요지. ⑤가 정답.
gist.distractor_ko: ①추천 추종, ②기술 객관성, ③이론 무용론, ④예측 신뢰는 모두 본문 주장과 반대다.

passage: Every choice happens somewhere, and where it happens changes what gets chosen.
Online, algorithms build that somewhere for us.
They curate the feed, the recommendation, and the menu of options itself.
In doing so they nudge us, sometimes gently and sometimes not, toward particular paths.
A nudge toward exercise is welcome; a nudge that serves only the platform is not.
Keeping our judgment intact demands a conscious, continuing effort.
It means hunting for perspectives the feed hides and choosing against the predicted grain.
It means treating an algorithm's output as a picture of yesterday, not a prescription for tomorrow.
choices: Faster Algorithms, Smarter Shopping Carts
Who Designs Your Choices? Reclaiming Judgment Online
The Rise and Fall of Behavioral Economics
Data Never Lies: Trusting the Numbers
How Platforms Compete for Advertising Revenue
title.explanation_ko: 누가 우리의 선택 환경을 설계하는가를 묻고, 그 안에서 판단력을 되찾는 방법을 제시하는 글이다. ②가 제목.
title.distractor_ko: ①쇼핑 효율, ③학문사, ④데이터 신뢰, ⑤광고 경쟁은 글의 결론과 어긋나거나 다룬 바 없다.

passage: It is comfortable to believe that our online choices are entirely our own.
In truth, the environment in which those choices are made is designed by algorithms.
They curate what appears, what is recommended, and what options exist at all.
Even a well-meant nudge narrows the range of paths we can see.
When the designer's goals diverge from ours, that narrowing becomes manipulation.
We cannot expect the system to correct itself on our behalf.
Users must therefore seek out perspectives the feed never offers and make choices against its predictions.
Only such deliberate resistance keeps human agency alive in an algorithmic world.
choices: 알고리즘의 추천 정확도를 높이는 연구에 투자해야 한다.
디지털 기기 사용 시간을 정해 두고 엄격히 지켜야 한다.
플랫폼 기업의 데이터 수집을 법으로 전면 금지해야 한다.
알고리즘의 추천에 의식적으로 맞서며 주체적으로 선택해야 한다.
행동경제학 이론을 학교 교육과정에 반드시 포함해야 한다.
claim.explanation_ko: 마지막 두 문장이 주장이다. 알고리즘의 예측에 맞서 의도적으로 선택함으로써 주체성을 지키라는 ④가 정답.
claim.distractor_ko: ①추천 개선, ②사용 시간, ③법적 금지, ⑤교육과정은 본문이 권하는 대응이 아니다.

passage: Choice architecture describes how a decision environment shapes the decisions made within it.
Algorithms are the architects of the digital environments we now inhabit.
They curate what we see, what we are recommended, and what options reach us at all.
Their nudges may be helpful, but they may also serve goals that are not ours.
Cultivating human agency therefore requires conscious, critical engagement.
It means seeking out diverse perspectives and choosing against the predicted grain.
It means treating an algorithm's confident output as one voice, not the final word.
Above all, it means refusing to walk only the corridors that were built for us.

summary.summary_template: Because algorithms __(A)__ the digital environments in which we choose, preserving human agency requires that we deliberately __(B)__ the paths they recommend.
summary.explanation_ko: 알고리즘은 우리가 선택하는 환경을 (A)design(설계)하므로, 주체성을 지키려면 그들이 권하는 경로에 의도적으로 (B)resist(저항)해야 한다. ⑤가 정답.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)에 measure·ignore는 '설계자(architects)'라는 본문의 은유와 맞지 않고, (B)에 follow는 '예측된 방향에 거스르라'는 결론과 정반대다.

writing.answer: 이러한 자극이 더 건강한 습관을 장려하는 것처럼 이로운 목적에 쓰일 수도 있지만, 그것들은 조작의 가능성도 함께 지닌다.

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 본문 내용을 바탕으로 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 한 단어씩 쓰시오. (본문의 표현을 그대로 옮기지 않아도 됨)
writing.summary: Because algorithms (A)___________ the digital environments in which our choices are made, keeping human agency alive requires us to (B)___________ the paths they quietly recommend.
writing.explanation_ko: (A) 알고리즘은 디지털 환경의 architects이므로 design(설계하다). (B) 예측된 방향에 거스르는 선택을 하라는 결론이므로 resist(저항하다).
